title: Reliability Workbench: Sprint Tiles, Stakeholder Risks, and SLO Gate Plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a working plan for a cross-functional reliability program called the ‘Reliability Workbench’. Focus: standardize SLO definitions, align telemetry and alerting, create a sprint-based runway for incremental SLO adoption, and run controlled error-budget experiments across product, serving-runtime, infra, and console teams.

Audience:
SREs, product owners, platform and infra engineers, observability, and release managers. Use as a coordination artifact for the next 8 weeks and as the source for a public-facing runbook afterwards.

High-level goals (MUST):
- Ship consistent SLO templates and three service-level contracts (latency, availability, correctness) for 6 pilot services.
- Instrument the canonical telemetry (p50/p90/p99 latency, request success rate, NDU for inference requests, tail backpressure indicators) and create one unified dashboard per pilot.
- Define and trial an error-budget policy and canary gating mechanism for model rollouts.
- Run two error-budget experiments and capture impact on cost/latency/quality.

Non-goals:
- Sweeping infra refactors. Keep changes incremental; prefer platform-level toggles over large code rewrites.
- Enterprise legal/compliance approvals (those follow after technical gates).

Success metrics (what we’ll measure):
- Template adoption: SLO templates applied to 6 pilot services within 8 weeks.
- Observability coverage: >=95% of SLO signal dimensions emitting for pilots (latency, success rate, error types, queue depth).
- Canary gate effectiveness: at least one rollback triggered by canary that prevented incorrect rollout.
- Reduced incident volume: 15% fewer P1s for pilot services during the experiment window (compared to prior 90 days).

Program cadence and roles:
- Weekly reliability sync (30 min): SRE leads + product owners + telemetry engineer — review dashboards, open blockers. Owner: Asha Patel.
- Bi-weekly risk retro (60 min): cross-functional recap of experiments, decisions, and postmortems. Owner: Jordan Lee.
- Daily short standups for implementation sprints (optional, team-driven).
- Decision authority: Product owner owns SLA tradeoffs; SRE owns error-budget policy enforcement; Platform Eng owns rollout automation.

Stakeholder matrix (quick):
- Product-hosted-api: Owner Nora Martinez — define correctness SLOs and customer-impact thresholds.
- Serving-runtime: Diego Alvarez — implement runtime metrics and KV cache telemetry hooks.
- Platform/infra: Liam O'Connor — ensure autoscaling and capacity annotations.
- Observability: Priya Sharma — dashboard templates, alerting rules, query ownership.

Sprint plan (8-week runway, 2-week sprints):
- Sprint 0 (week 0): Kickoff, pick 6 pilots, baseline telemetry audit (+run vulnerability checklist). Deliverables: pilot list, baseline dashboards, measurement gaps.
- Sprint 1: SLO templates finalized, raw metrics plumbing to telemetry, low-friction dashboard for p50/p90/p99 and success rate. Deliverables: SLO doc, dashboard v1.
- Sprint 2: Implement error-budget policy automation (alerts + gating hook), create canary pipeline for model versions. Deliverables: error budget spec, canary playbook.
- Sprint 3: Run first error-budget experiment (controlled traffic shift to a variant with instrumentation). Capture metrics & incidents. Deliverables: experiment log, metrics snapshot.
- Sprint 4: Incorporate learnings, refine alerts (reduce noise), instrument service-specific correctness signals. Deliverables: alert tuning PRs, correctness metrics.
- Sprint 5: Run second experiment (stress/backpressure scenario simulation). Evaluate rollback triggers and cost delta. Deliverables: stress test report, rollback playbook.
- Sprint 6: Draft cross-team runbook, operational escalation flows, and SLO onboarding checklist. Deliverables: runbook draft, onboarding checklist.
- Sprint 7: Finalize documentation, exec summary, and handoff to service teams for steady-state. Deliverables: final runbook, postmortem & next-step backlog.

SLO definitions (templates):
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile <= X ms for inference endpoint under production mix. Definition: rolling 7d window, 72% target (configurable per tier).
- Availability SLO: 99.95% of requests return a valid inference response (no upstream timeouts) over 30d. Error taxonomy: client errors (4xx) excluded; internal errors and timeouts included.
- Correctness SLO: pass-rate on a small deterministic eval set >= threshold (service-specific). Check executed on canary and daily batch checks on anchored prompts.

Instrumentation checklist (minimum signals):
- Request ingress timestamps, server-side latency, downstream RPC latencies, KV cache hit/miss, queue length/backpressure, model version tag, error type labels, sample traces for p99.
- Alerts: burst-latency anomaly, sustained p99 breach >10m, error-rate spike >2x baseline, error-budget burn rate >2x for 30m.

Error-budget policy (short):
- Burn rate calculation: burn = (observed_slo_violation / allowed_violation) normalized over window.
- Thresholds: advisory @ burn 0.8, escalated @ burn 1.5, forced mitigation (throttle/rollback) @ burn 2.5.
- Manual override: Product can pause mitigation for business reasons but must log decision in decision log with reasoning and acceptance of residual risk.

Canary gating and rollout policy (overview):
- Canary sequence: deploy canary + 3% traffic for 30 min -> observe correctness signals and telemetry -> if no advisory alerts escalate -> increase to 15% for 60 min -> if steady -> full rollout.
- Automated rollback triggers: sustained p99 latency > threshold for 15 min OR correctness SLO on canary below minimum OR error-rate spike above configured threshold.

Experiment templates (runbook lines):
- Pre-experiment checklist: baseline snapshot, alert mute matrix, rollback validation, stakeholder notify list.
- Data capture: capture raw traces, sampling config for p99, event of rollback.
- Post: timeline of events, root cause if rollback occurs, cost delta analysis.

Risk register (top items and mitigations):
- Risk: Alert fatigue from naive p99 alerts. Mitigation: phased alert tuning; use burn-rate rather than immediate P1.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps in legacy services. Mitigation: lightweight proxy metric shim and short-term sampling.
- Risk: Canary sampling not representative. Mitigation: traffic shaping + synthetic requests to exercise edge paths.
- Risk: Cost spike during experiments. Mitigation: cap traffic and set budget alerts; run during low-cost windows.

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Final numeric SLO thresholds for p99 latency (product to propose by 2026-02-12).
- Which 6 pilots (list proposed; needs sign-off).
- Default retention window for SLO telemetry (90d vs 30d) — telemetry to recommend.

Meeting artifacts / docs to produce:
- One-pager exec summary for GTM and customer success explaining error-budget policy and rollback impact.
- Public runbook (internal-facing) with step-by-step canary rollback commands and owner contact list.
- Decision log (append to this doc) with date, decision, owners, links.

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Lock pilot services list (Asha + Nora)
2) Telemetry gap audit (Priya) — deliverable EOD Wed
3) Prototype SLO template in Confluence (Jordan)
4) Infra checklist for canary automation (Diego + Liam)
5) Schedule kickoff + 1st weekly reliability sync (calendar invite out)

Notes to self / rapid ideas (scratch):
- Consider cost-aware canaries: route cheaper quantized model variant for 5% of traffic to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Add a tiny synthetic workload generator to exercise cold-starts in serving-runtime.
- Use feature flags to toggle canary gating on a per-team basis so early adopters can opt-in.

Appendix: templates/links (scratch):
- Baseline dashboard query (promql snippet) -> CONF-RELIABILITY-87
- Error-budget calc spreadsheet -> CLOUD-1234
- Canary pipeline PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/432

Reminder: this is a working document. Expect changes after sprint 1. Add decision records and link PRs/Jira tickets so we can version the runbook.
